title: Edge Notifications Keep Appearing After Closing the Browser: Block One Website
description: Stop one website's notifications in Microsoft Edge. Understand how site permissions differ from closing the browser or switching off Windows notifications.

sections.heading: Closing Edge does not necessarily stop website notifications
paragraphs: Microsoft says a website you have allowed to send notifications can continue displaying them after Edge is closed. An absent browser window does not, by itself, identify a different source.

This guide covers unwanted website notifications on a Windows PC. Start by checking the app name and website address on the message. In Windows 11, you can open Notification Center from the taskbar or with Windows key + N.

sections.heading: Block the sender in Edge settings
paragraphs: Open Edge directly instead of following an unfamiliar security alert. Microsoft lists the following route in its official instructions, checked on October 17, 2026.
bullets: Open the three-dot menu in Edge's upper-right corner and choose Settings.
Open Privacy, search, and services, then Site permissions, then All sites.
Select the website whose alerts you want to stop.
Find its Notifications permission and change the selection to Block.

sections.heading: Dismissing a message is different from blocking its sender
paragraphs: Clearing an item from Notification Center removes that displayed message. To stop future notifications from a website, check that its notification permission is set to Block.
If you accidentally block a useful site, you can change its permission back to Allow in the same menu. You do not need to revisit a suspicious website to manage its saved permission.

sections.heading: When to use Windows notification settings
paragraphs: Windows 11 also offers notification controls under Start, Settings, System, Notifications. Choose the scope that matches your problem: one website, one app, or notifications across Windows.
bullets: Block one website in Edge when a particular sender is the problem.
Turn off Edge's app notifications in Windows, if Edge appears in the app list, when you want to suppress notifications from that app more broadly. Useful browser alerts may disappear too.
Turn off all Windows notifications only when you intend to affect other apps as well.
Use Do Not Disturb to reduce interruptions. Do not treat it as revoking a website's saved notification permission.

sections.heading: Treat alarming security wording as a claim to check
paragraphs: The Edge team has described websites that solicit notification permission and then send messages made to look like security warnings. The wording alone does not establish that Windows has detected a problem.
bullets: If you only saw the message, inspect the sender's permission instead of following its scan or installation instructions.
If you installed software or entered account details, blocking notifications is not a complete response. The appropriate next steps depend on what you actually did.

sections.heading: If messages continue after the change
paragraphs: Compare the app name and website address on each new notification with the sender you blocked. Similar-looking names can refer to different sources. Identify the source before changing permissions for unrelated websites.
This article is based on official documentation. The steps have not been independently reproduced on a physical PC. Menu placement can vary with the Edge version and interface language.
